entries.english:
Concerning the castle of Liechtenstein. An exemplification taken from the original, word for word and by the authority granted to me, the notary Aycardus set out below, by the venerable father and lord Henry, by the grace of God bishop of Trento, in the year of the Lord 1277, indiction five, on Thursday, the second day of December, at Trento in the episcopal palace, in the presence of Lords Herardus of Tyngwestang, captain of Trento; Jordan of Gardumo; Aprowinus of Borgo Nuovo; Olricus of Bolzano; Master Peter the physician; Tridentinus the notary; and other witnesses.

In the name of the Lord. On Tuesday, the thirteenth day before the end of April, in the presence of Master Romaninus; Rodegerius, parish priest of Marniga; Lord Girardus, court judge; Lord Baldricus, advocate; Artuicus, Gotsalc, Varnardus and Federicus of Weineck; Henry of Rosenpach; Purchardus of Seben; Gotçalch and Federicus of Castelrotto; Henry of Salech; Viliemis of Valturnes; Zuco and Hegino of Firmian; and many others.

Lord Conrad, elected bishop of the see of Trento, who had already received the regalia from the hand of Lord Emperor Frederick, invested Lady Adleita, daughter of the late Gothsalc of Castelrotto, her son Henry, and Otto the younger, son of the late Herkempret of Weineck and her husband, with the proper fief specifically consisting of the wardship and custody of the castle of Liechtenstein. Thus, from that day onward, whoever of the aforesaid persons survived was to hold the wardship and custody of the castle of Liechtenstein as a proper fief from the aforesaid lord elect and his successors in perpetuity. Adleita, Henry and Otto, or whichever of them survived, were to guard the aforesaid castle of Liechtenstein faithfully and without fraud, for the honor of the bishop of Trento, so that it should always and at all times be open to the aforesaid bishop elect and his successors in the bishopric for all their affairs. For so they agreed.

This was done successfully at Bolzano, in the house of the lord bishop. In the year of the Lord’s nativity 1189, indiction seven. I, Albert, notary of Lord Emperor Frederick and of the court of Trento, was present and wrote this charter. I, Aycardus of Amichis of Dosso, notary, faithfully copied this original exemplification by the aforesaid authority and mandate, placed my sign, and subscribed at the request of the parties. I, Zacheus, notary of the Sacred Palace, saw and read the original of this exemplification; as it was contained there, so it is faithfully read in this copy; I placed my sign and subscribed. I, Tridentinus, notary of Lord Bishop Egno of Trento, saw and read the original of this exemplification; as it was contained there, so it is faithfully read in this copy; I placed my sign and subscribed.
